standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the cone c(delta[-1]) with its structure maps i and p whose triangle is compared with the rotated admissible triangle.

core_obligations: The comparison maps (proof lines 4183-4192): with splittings tilde-alpha, tilde-beta of alpha, beta and tilde-i, tilde-p of i, p displayed in the two-row diagram, define y to c(delta[-1]) by i tilde-alpha + tilde-p beta and c(delta[-1]) to y by alpha tilde-i + tilde-beta p.

Differential closedness (proof lines 4193-4214): using the delta[-1] identities from lemma-get-triangle one derives d(tilde-alpha) = -delta[-1] beta and d(tilde-p) = i delta[-1]; expanding d(i tilde-alpha + tilde-p beta) then telescopes to -i delta[-1] beta + i delta[-1] beta = 0, and a similar computation shows alpha tilde-i + tilde-beta p is also a morphism of Comp(A); the two maps fit in the commutative diagram.

The composition identities (proof lines 4215-4237): expanding (i tilde-alpha + tilde-p beta)(alpha tilde-i + tilde-beta p) with the lemma-get-triangle identities collapses to i tilde-i + tilde-p p = 1 on the cone, and the reverse composite equals 1 on y; hence y is isomorphic to c(delta[-1]) and the two triangles are isomorphic.
proof_roadmap: Write the two-row comparison diagram with all splittings and define the two comparison maps from them.
Check both maps are closed morphisms using the splitting identities, and note the diagram commutes.
Compose both ways, collapse the products with the lemma-get-triangle identities, and conclude the triangle isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the rotated admissible triangle with the cone triangle of the rotated differential (statement lines 4166-4180). The proof (lines 4182-4254) is a hands-on computation in the differential graded category: the comparison maps are built from the splittings, their closedness follows from the delta[-1] identities of lemma-get-triangle with an explicit telescoping differential computation, and the two composition expansions collapse to the identity through the same identities. H2: every identity is displayed and verified in the span, and the result is the engine behind the rotation axiom verifications elsewhere in the chapter.
